name: MAX22201ATC+T
title: MAX22201/MAX22202/MAX22207: 36 V, 3.5 A brushed DC motor H-bridge with integrated current sense
summary: One full H-bridge rated to 36 V for a single brushed DC motor, one phase of a stepper, or a latching valve or solenoid. The bridge FETs total 0.3 Ω typ (high side plus low side); peak current is bounded by the 3.5 A minimum overcurrent threshold and continuous current is 2 A rms on a JEDEC four-layer board at 25 °C. Current is measured losslessly in the low-side FETs: a resistor on ILIM sets a peak current the chip regulates with a fixed off time, and ISEN sources 1/5000 of the output current. MAX22201 has IN1/IN2 inputs and a resistor-set off time, MAX22202 has PHASE/ENBL/MODE inputs, and MAX22207 has IN1/IN2 inputs and a CDROUT flag; all come in a 12-pin 3 mm x 3 mm TDFN.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, MAX22201
circuits.description: A controller drives the motor through IN1 and IN2 and watches FAULT, which is pulled up to the logic rail. RILIM on ILIM sets the peak current the chip holds the motor to; RROFF on ROFF sets the off time of that regulation. An optional RISEN on ISEN gives the controller's ADC a voltage proportional to motor current. VM has 100 nF and a bulk capacitor, and V18 has 1 µF.

operation.text: The 3.5 A peak is the overcurrent threshold and holds only for short transients. The 2 A rms continuous figure is a thermal limit, quoted for a JEDEC four-layer board at 25 °C ambient; in a real design it depends on ground copper, heat sinking and airflow.

MAX22201 and MAX22207 take two PWM inputs, IN1 and IN2, giving four states: forward, reverse, coast, and brake (slow decay). MAX22201 adds a resistor-set off time on ROFF. MAX22207 adds CDROUT, an open-drain output asserted while the internal current regulation has control. MAX22202 takes ENBL and PHASE, with MODE choosing slow or fast decay. Every version has overcurrent, thermal and undervoltage protection and an active-low open-drain FAULT output.

With IN1 and IN2 both low for longer than tSLEEP, the chip goes into sleep: outputs at high impedance, supply current ISLEEP of 6.5 µA max. Powering up with both inputs low puts it straight into sleep. Driving IN1 and IN2 both high for 400 µs or more wakes it.

Holding MODE high (brake) for longer than tSLEEP and then taking MODE low puts the MAX22202 to sleep, outputs at high impedance, with ISLEEP of 10 µA max. After power-up with MODE = 0 it sleeps at once. A MODE-high pulse of 400 µs or more (the tON maximum) wakes it.

1) PWM with regulation: ITRIP is set above the normal running current so it only clips start-up inrush, and the controller does speed or position control by PWM, normally braking (slow decay) in the off phase. 2) PWM without regulation: a 14 kΩ on ILIM disables the regulator, leaving the full 3.5 A available for short periods; uncontrolled current can then hit OCP or thermal shutdown. 3) Regulation only: the inputs just enable the bridge and set direction, and torque is set by ITRIP through RILIM, which may be changed on the fly. 4) PWM with ISEN feedback: as 1 or 2, with a resistor on ISEN giving the controller's ADC the motor current.

In brake (slow decay) both low-side FETs are on and short the winding, so current falls slowly; this is the usual off phase for brushed motors because ripple is lower and efficiency higher. Fast decay comes either from reversing the bridge (synchronous) or from turning it off so the current flows through the FET body diodes (asynchronous). On the MAX22202 the PWM can go on PHASE or on ENBL; with ENBL, MODE decides between fast decay and brake.

Current is measured with sense-FETs in each of the two low-side FETs, so no sense resistor is needed and the measurement costs no power. It is measured while the bridge drives forward or reverse and during brake; during fast decay it is not measured and ISEN gives zero.

When the output current passes ITRIP (set by RILIM, Equation 1) the chip forces slow decay, both low-side FETs on, for the fixed off time tOFF: 20 µs typ on MAX22202 and MAX22207, set by ROFF on MAX22201. The loop controls the peak current, so the average depends on the ripple. If the inputs stay steady, slow decay lasts the whole tOFF; a PWM edge during tOFF resets the timer and hands the bridge back to the inputs. At the end of tOFF the inputs take over if the current is below ITRIP, otherwise another tOFF follows. While limiting, the output duty cycle and frequency depend on supply voltage, motor inductance, tOFF and motor speed. The function caps inrush at start-up and in stall, easing supply and bypass needs.

ISEN sources IOUT / KISEN whenever a low-side FET carries the output current, which covers the on phase and brake. A resistor RISEN from ISEN to GND makes a voltage for an ADC, chosen by Equation 4 so the peak fits full scale; RISEN is also the output impedance of the monitor. An ADC with high input impedance connects directly; a low-impedance ADC may need a buffer. The ISEN voltage range is 0 V to 1.2 V.

CDROUT is open drain and needs a pull-up to the controller's logic supply. It stays high while the motor current is under ITRIP in forward or reverse, and goes low when the regulator forces slow decay. A slow decay commanded on IN1 and IN2 does not pull it low. Any PWM edge restarts the off timer, so the real brake interval can end before tOFF or run past it.

Shorts to supply, to ground and across the outputs are caught when the current reaches the OCP threshold (3.5 A min): FAULT asserts and the bridge turns off for tRETRY, 2 ms, then comes back according to the inputs. A persisting short repeats the cycle. Long operation in this auto-retry state may harm reliability and is to be avoided.
Above about 165 °C die temperature FAULT asserts and the bridge goes to high impedance; it is enabled again once the junction cools below 135 °C.
VM UVLO is 3 V max. Under UVLO FAULT asserts and the outputs go to high impedance; when the supply returns to its operating range the chip resumes and FAULT releases.
OUT1 and OUT2 are rated 8 kV HBM, and 10 kV HBM once the part is soldered to a board carrying 1 µF or more of VM bypass.
